How to Buy on Telegram

The order matters more than any single step. Run it in sequence and stop at the first failure.

The sequence

  1. Ask which office issued it and confirm the answer is the issuing office.
  2. Request an uncropped photo of the full card on a plain surface with the laminate edge in frame.
  3. Request a UV shot of the data page and a close crop of the number field.
  4. Test the number against the format the issuing office uses. A number that breaks the format ends the deal.
  5. Agree a price inside the the observed band local currency band and pay in two parts, deposit then balance against tracking.
  6. On arrival check the document against the photos before you accept delivery and photograph the unopened envelope.

Why the order is fixed

Each step is a small payment of trust the seller has to earn before the next. Photos before payment, number before balance, tracking before the second half. Reversing any two of those moves risk onto you.

Payment

Split it. A third up, two thirds against a tracking number that actually moves. Crypto is fine at that split, never for the whole amount.

On arrival

Photograph the unopened envelope, then the document beside it. Check against the photos before you accept. If the document is wrong, the envelope ties it to the seller.

The generic checks

  • Check the number format against the published rule for the issuing office. Constructed numbers cannot be invented by hand.
  • Look for the UV print with a 365 nanometre torch. Real ink is sharp and placed deliberately. A print shows a dull bloom or nothing.
  • Loupe the microprint and the ghost image. Both collapse into a dotted line or a grey patch on a photocopy.
  • Compare the data across every field for internal consistency. A postcode that contradicts the state or the office area is a tell.
  • Check the laminate or polycarbonate edge for a fused seal rather than a cut line under a laid sheet.

The generic red flags

  • The seller cannot name the issuing office, only the country.
  • The number breaks the published format, or is round and repeating.
